description:
FILED s507c (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-05) from #2690's -c probes; PRE-EXISTING on main ac2fec1e (and on the plain run, not only -c).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):
  perl -e 'use List::Util; print 0+$!, "\n"; die "x\n"'; echo $?    -> x / 2 / rc=2
  pcl  -e 'use List::Util; print 0+$!, "\n"; die "x\n"'; echo $?    -> x / 0 / rc=255
  perl -e 'use strict; print 0+$!, "\n"; die "x\n"'                 -> 0 / rc=255   (strict.pm is found in the FIRST @INC dir)
  and under -c: printf 'use List::Util qw(sum);\nBEGIN { die "begin died\n" }\n' > c7.pl; perl -c c7.pl -> rc 2, pcl -c c7.pl -> rc 255.

CAUSE (read, the cheap measurement is the third line above): perl's `require` walks @INC and every directory that does not hold the file leaves ENOENT in errno; a later `die` exits with $! when it is nonzero.  PCL's module search (p-find-module-in-inc) probes with probe-file, which never touches PCL's *p-stored-errno*, so $! stays 0 and an uncaught die exits 255.
An exit status a shell script or a test harness reads: an everyday program that `use`s a module from a later @INC directory and then dies exits 2 under perl and 255 under PCL.
FIX DIRECTION: the search records ENOENT in $! (the %p-io-errno-fail 2 the failure path already uses) when it had to skip at least one directory -- measure which @INC position perl's own modules sit in (List::Util is in the arch dir, strict in lib/) and probe `$!` after `use` for three modules at three positions.

=== MEASURED, NOT SHIPPED (s508a, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-05) ===
The fix direction above ("the @INC search records ENOENT when it had to skip at least one directory") is CONTRADICTED by perl itself.  Measured with perl 5.40.3 (`perl -e 'use M; print 0+$!'`, @INC = site_perl/arch, site_perl, lib/arch, lib), probe scratch/s508a/probes/errno-probe.pl in the s508a worktree:

  $! = 0 although the module sits PAST the first @INC dir: strict, warnings, Carp, Exporter, constant, Tie::Hash, Text::Tabs, Getopt::Long, File::Temp, JSON::PP (all in lib/, the 4th), File::Spec, POSIX, Data::Dumper, Time::HiRes (lib/arch, the 3rd), Moo (site_perl, the 2nd).
  $! = 2: List::Util, Scalar::Util, Cwd, Storable, Digest::MD5 (lib/arch), Text::Wrap (lib), PPI (site_perl).
  `$! = 5; require strict` -> 0 and `$! = 5; require Tie::Hash` -> 0, while `$! = 5; eval "1"` -> 5.

So a SUCCESSFUL require leaves errno 0 at the point the file is opened (the failed probes of earlier @INC dirs do not survive), and the final $! is whatever a failing system call INSIDE the module's own load left behind: XSLoader/DynaLoader's shared-object search for List::Util / Scalar::Util / Cwd / Storable / Digest::MD5 (POSIX and Time::HiRes come out 0), a utf8/unicore file lookup or similar for Text::Wrap (its dependencies alone -- warnings::register, Exporter, Text::Tabs -- each leave 0), something in PPI's tree.  PCL loads shims for most of these (List::Util is a must-win shim and never runs XSLoader), so its $! cannot follow the module internals that set it.

What the ruled direction would do: make strict / Carp / Exporter / Getopt::Long / File::Temp / JSON::PP / constant (rc 255 in perl after a die) exit 2 -- a NEW divergence on the commonest modules, to fix the List::Util one.  Not shipped.  A narrower candidate that IS consistent with the table: a successful require sets $! = 0 (perl's own reset) -- that alone changes nothing for the reported case (it is already 0 in PCL).  The reported row (List::Util then die -> rc 2) would need the XS-shim modules to leave ENOENT as XSLoader does in perl, which is module behaviour (rule 9a: it would live in the shims, e.g. lib/List/Util.pm setting $! = 2 at the end of its load) -- that is a USER call, because it encodes an accident of perl's XS loader as data.
subject: A die after a `use` of a module found past the first @INC directory exits 2 under perl ($! is the ENOENT the @INC search left) and 255 under PCL ($! stays 0) -- `perl -e 'use List::Util; die "x\n"'` rc 2, pcl rc 255; also `pcl -c` on a dying BEGIN (PRE-EXISTING, found by s507c)
